stemMd: Why does a damaged heart valve reduce the efficiency of blood pumping?

options.label: A
options.textMd: It can allow backflow that reduces net forward movement.

options.label: B
options.textMd: It causes every artery to carry air instead of blood.

options.label: C
options.textMd: It removes the need for pressure differences.

options.label: D
options.textMd: It changes all blood into lymph immediately.

explanationMd: Valves maintain one-way flow by opening and closing in response to pressure differences. A valve that does not close properly permits regurgitation, so part of a contraction moves blood backward instead of delivering it forward. The effect follows from fluid direction, not a change in blood’s identity.

distractorRationale.d: Valve damage does not directly transform blood into lymph.
distractorRationale.e: Haemoglobin remains present in red blood cells.
distractorRationale.c: Blood flow still depends on pressure differences.
distractorRationale.b: This is not the consequence of ordinary valve malfunction.
